answer: Persistent handle ledger. Each identity gets a unique, costly-to-replace handle recorded in an append-only public log, so a duplicate clone leaves a visible ledge in the record that others can check before transacting. Any new handle must reference an existing one, and the reference creates a ripple through prior history that exposes copied behavior patterns. Attackers pay recurring storage and verification costs per handle, and a cloned identity must also fund a distinct nebula of activity records to avoid matching, raising the per-account price above its expected value.
